title: Underived presheaf pushforward base change for fibred groupoids
statement: Fix the universes and small-skeleton convention of [def-weil-size-convention] and a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme]. Let $v:\mathcal C\to\mathcal X$ and $b:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal X$ be functors over $\mathit{Sch}/S$ between categories fibred in groupoids [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], and let $\mathcal C'=\mathcal Y\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal C$ with projections $a:\mathcal C'\to\mathcal C$ and $v':\mathcal C'\to\mathcal Y$. Let $N$ be an abelian presheaf on $\mathcal C$, meaning a contravariant functor to abelian groups [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For any functor between such categories $w:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ over $S$, define $w^{-1}$ by precomposition and $(w_*M)(z)=\Gamma((\mathit{Sch}/T)\times_{z,\mathcal B}\mathcal A,M|_{(\mathit{Sch}/T)\times_{z,\mathcal B}\mathcal A})$ for $z$ over $T$; the restriction of $M$ is precomposition, $\Gamma$ is the group of families compatible with every arrow, and restrictions of $w_*M$ are restriction of families along test-fibre functors. There is a canonical natural isomorphism of abelian presheaves $\beta_N:b^{-1}v_*N\xrightarrow{\sim}v'_*a^{-1}N$. Its component at $y$ over $T$ restricts a compatible family along the canonical functor $(\mathit{Sch}/T)\times_{y,\mathcal Y}\mathcal C'\to(\mathit{Sch}/T)\times_{b(y),\mathcal X}\mathcal C$, using the specified two-isomorphism $va\cong bv'$ to identify coefficient values. The isomorphism is natural in $N$ and commutes with restriction along every arrow of $\mathcal Y$. The assertion also applies to any specified $2$-cartesian square with these sides. No sheaf, algebraicity, or representability hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 075B (lemma-base-change), proof using the test-fibre equivalence; holds for abelian presheaves by applying the displayed compatible-family bijection componentwise.

proof.text: Use the definitions of fibred groupoid and fibrewise $2$-product in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Write $J_y$ for pairs $(c,\alpha:v(c)\to b(y))$, with arrows $t:c\to c_1$ satisfying $\alpha_1v(t)=\alpha$. This is a concrete presentation of the test fibre: for $u:U\to T$, choose a lift $u^*b(y)\to b(y)$; its cartesian factorization property identifies an arrow $v(c)\to b(y)$ over $u$ with a vertical isomorphism $v(c)\cong u^*b(y)$. Changing the lift gives its unique vertical comparison, so the coefficient remains $N(c)$, with restriction $N(t)$. Similarly present the other test fibre by $K_y$, whose objects are $(y_0,c,\theta,\delta)$, where $\theta:b(y_0)\xrightarrow{\sim}v(c)$ is vertical and $\delta:y_0\to y$. An arrow is $(s,t)$ with $\delta_1s=\delta$ and $v(t)\theta=\theta_1b(s)$. Define $H_y:K_y\to J_y$ by $(y_0,c,\theta,\delta)\mapsto(c,b(\delta)\theta^{-1})$ and $(s,t)\mapsto t$. These equations verify that this is a functor and that its coefficient diagram is exactly the restriction of the diagram $N(c)$ on $J_y$.

source.place: Tag 075B, lemma-base-change; equation-pushforward immediately before it

proof.text: The functor $H_y$ is fully faithful and essentially surjective, directly by [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Given $t:H_y(k)\to H_y(k_1)$, the base arrows satisfy $p(\delta_1)p(t)=p(\delta)$. Cartesian factorization through $\delta_1$ gives a unique $s:y_0\to y_1$ over $p(t)$ with $\delta_1s=\delta$. The equation for $t$ implies $b(\delta_1)b(s)=b(\delta_1)\theta_1^{-1}v(t)\theta$; cartesian uniqueness through $b(\delta_1)$ makes the two factors equal, giving the required square. Thus $(s,t)$ exists uniquely. For $(c,\alpha)\in J_y$, lift the base arrow of $\alpha$ to $\delta:y_0\to y$. The arrow $b(\delta)$ is cartesian, since every arrow of a fibred groupoid has the defining factorization property. Hence $\alpha=b(\delta)\lambda$ uniquely, with $\lambda:v(c)\to b(y_0)$ vertical and therefore invertible. Take $\theta=\lambda^{-1}$; its image under $H_y$ is $(c,\alpha)$.

source.place: Tag 075B, lemma-base-change; equation-pushforward immediately before it

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-initial-functor-limit] to $H_y^{\mathrm{op}}$ and to the set-valued diagram underlying $N(c)$. Its initiality hypothesis holds: full faithfulness and an isomorphism $H_y(k_0)\cong j$ make the comma category of arrows $H_y^{\mathrm{op}}(k)\to j$ have a terminal object $(k_0,\epsilon^{\mathrm{op}})$; the unique arrow to it is the lift, by full faithfulness, of the required composite with $\epsilon^{-1}$. A category with a terminal object is nonempty and any two objects are connected through that object, as required by the cited statement. The set of compatible families is a limit: its projections form a cone, and a cone from a set $A$ factors uniquely by sending each $a\in A$ to its tuple of projected values. Consequently the cited canonical limit comparison is the bijection $s\mapsto(s_{H_y(k)})_k$. Both groups in the item are these compatible-family groups; this bijection is the specified component $\beta_N(y)$.

source.place: Tag 075B, lemma-base-change; equation-pushforward immediately before it

proof.text: Addition, zero and negatives of compatible families are coordinatewise, so the displayed restriction bijection is additive and its inverse is additive. For a morphism $\eta:N\to N_1$, its two composites with $\beta$ have value $\eta_c(s_{H_y(k)})$ at $k$, proving naturality in coefficients. For an arrow $r:y'\to y$, the test-fibre functors send $\alpha$ to $b(r)\alpha$ and $\delta$ to $r\delta$. The equality $b(r\delta)\theta^{-1}=b(r)(b(\delta)\theta^{-1})$ shows that both composites of restriction with $\beta$ evaluate $s$ at the very same object of $J_y$, with the same coefficient value. Thus $\beta$ is a morphism of abelian presheaves. The inverses of these component bijections commute with restrictions by composing this equality with the inverses, hence give its presheaf inverse.

source.place: Tag 075B, lemma-base-change; equation-pushforward immediately before it

proof.text: For a specified $2$-cartesian square with upper-left category $D$, the specified comparison $E:D\to\mathcal Y\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal C$ is an equivalence over the base and the sides, with their specified natural isomorphisms. It induces an equivalence of the test categories over each $y$: full faithfulness lifts arrows uniquely, and an isomorphism $E(d)\cong k$ transports the structural arrow $k\to y$ to give an object over $y$. These are the same full-faithfulness and essential-surjectivity checks as in step 2, with the side isomorphisms inserted. The coefficient diagrams agree by their specified isomorphism to $N(a(d))$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-initial-functor-limit] to the opposite of this equivalence exactly as in step 3. Restriction along it is a bijection on compatible families. Compose it with the component already constructed. The component is restriction along the composite test-fibre functor, using the given $va\cong bv'$. Naturality in $N$ follows by evaluating $\eta$ on that coefficient. For $r:y'\to y$, postcomposition of structural arrows commutes with $E$; naturality of the side isomorphisms makes the coefficient transports agree. Therefore the coordinate equality of step 4 still holds. This proves every clause for the specified square without any topology or representability assumption.
